title: After the Apostles — certainty only from what is written; no more ἀδιάπτωτοι
source_text: XXXV. Denique, quod praecipuum est, & unde reliqua sequuntur, illud constanter affirmamus eorum quae Apostoli docuerunt, aut instituerunt, nihil nos pro omnino certo & comperto habere, nisi ea quae sunt tradita & consignata in sacris literis. Et hoc quia post Apostolos, & viros Apostolicos, nulli amplius fuerunt in Ecclesia viri ἀδιάπτωτοι extra omne erroris periculum positi. Adeoque quicquid de dictis & factis Apostolorum, praeter scripta Canonica, ad nos usque pervenit, non habemus nisi ex fide hominum infirmorum, qui & falli & fallere potuerunt.
pass_a_gloss: Finally, which is the chief point, and whence the rest follow, we constantly affirm that of those things which the Apostles taught or instituted, we have nothing as altogether certain and ascertained except those which are handed down and consigned in the sacred letters. And this because after the Apostles and apostolic men, there were no longer in the Church men ἀδιάπτωτοι placed beyond every danger of error. And therefore whatever concerning the sayings and deeds of the Apostles, besides the Canonical writings, has come down to us, we have only from the faith of weak men, who both could be deceived and could deceive.
pass_b_english: The chief point — from which the rest follow — is this: of what the Apostles taught or instituted, we hold nothing as fully certain except what is handed down and set in sacred Scripture.

After the Apostles and apostolic men, the Church had no more ἀδιάπτωτοι men set beyond every danger of error. So whatever of their sayings and deeds reaches us outside the Canonical writings comes only on the credit of weak men, who could both err and deceive.

lemmas.gloss: to be deceived and to deceive

choices.why: Greek restored from broken OCR; technical for inspired immunity from error.
Paired with certo as epistemic closure.
